currentFocus.title: Design the Browser SQL target architecture from verified constraints and capabilities

stageSummary.completed: bootstrap, scope-definition, browser-sql-current-state-audit, browser-sql-requirements-consolidation, browser-sql-browser-constraints, browser-sql-official-capability-research
stageSummary.planned: relational model → ingest/atomicity → SQL scheduler → persistence/recovery → runtime delivery → viewer/results → testing → benchmark strategy → migration → failure/security/observability → implementation decomposition → GitHub execution structure → final plan audit

baselineSource.result: V1 remains the frozen verified reference for browser collection, integrity, atomic persistence behavior, viewer recovery and browser runtime patterns.

officialCapabilityResearch.result: Official current sources verify in-browser SQL, Worker execution, OPFS persistence capability, Arrow ingestion, required SQL features and documented Wasm constraints. Version-specific OPFS regression, multi-context concurrency, Leumi CSP compatibility, query cancellation and Market Flow-scale performance remain explicit unknowns.
keyGuardrails: Design for the single-threaded Wasm path first; coi threading is conditional and experimental.
Pin an exact tested duckdb-wasm version; do not float npm latest for persistence-critical use.
Require CHECKPOINT plus reopen/durability verification before OPFS becomes authoritative.
Do not assume multi-instance/cross-tab OPFS concurrency.
Do not depend on hard query cancellation until a Wasm API is verified.

engineSelection.note: Capability research supports proceeding to target architecture. Exact package version and production suitability remain later verification decisions.

verification.specImpact: No runtime behavior or normative Browser SQL spec changed. Phase D is research/planning evidence only.

next.action: Planning Phase E: design the Browser SQL target architecture.
steps: Choose the simplest single-authority browser topology for Collector, SQL Worker/database owner, scheduler and Viewer/result delivery.
Design for the single-threaded DuckDB-Wasm baseline; treat coi threading only as optional future optimization.
Preserve complete-cycle atomic visibility and one authoritative market-history source.
Decide where query execution and result delivery live without assuming unsupported cross-tab OPFS concurrency.
Define startup, normal ingest, scheduled query, query failure, Viewer refresh and recovery sequence flows.
Keep exact relational schema and detailed persistence/scheduler policy for their dedicated later phases.

history.rule: Superseded architecture/research plans remain cold history and do not carry current progress.
